title: How His Top Location Hit $7K a Month
excerpt: A Denver software sales manager started vending on paternity leave as an AI-layoff hedge, growing to about $43K a month across roughly 40 machines.
quote: I know any given month I'm going to land — if nothing else changed right now, I'd land between $42,000 and $43,000 to close out the month.
body:
## Background

Matt managed a sales team at a mid-size software company in Denver, work he describes as "single-minded, single-threaded in corporate land." He'd been laid off in tech before, and when his second child arrived he went on paternity leave and started looking for an alternative source of income, joining Vendingpreneurs in April 2024.

> We had our second child, and I went on paternity leave, and I was thinking, hey, let's work on an alternative source of income.

## The Challenge

The uncertainty around AI and tech layoffs was the trigger. Matt looked at Amazon reseller programs first but found them too intangible, worried about competing against sellers overseas who could undercut price on an algorithm he couldn't control. Real estate appealed to him too, since he'd dabbled in it before, but it was too capital intensive for what he wanted.

> What if I do lose my job, or what if AI ends up eliminating jobs — and we see that more and more every day? I was wanting to use it as like a hedge-of-the-bet type scenario.

## The Turning Point

Vending's tangibility and predictability won him over against the other, more intangible models he'd researched. His third location, which came together about four months in, was the moment it stopped feeling like a side project and he brought on his first stocker.

> In location three you're like, okay, this is real. I can't keep up myself. I want to bring someone else on that can support me here while I can... it shifts from solely operating to then optimizing, and then focusing on what I like to do, which is going out and talking to people and getting more locations.

## Where They Are Now

About two years in, Matt is installing his 21st location with around 40 machines, including micro markets, and revenue at about $43,000 a month, with a goal to double it by year's end. His top location, his third ever, brings in $6,500 to $7,000 a month. He held onto his W2 job for roughly 85 percent of the journey, treating vending as a hedge until it became a business in its own right.

> Eighty-five percent of the time I've had a W2 job while focusing on this. If I can do it, others can too.
review_notes: Matt states 'right at about 43,000 a month' directly; a separate predictability comment cites a $42-43K range for the same figure.
Location count: Matt says he is 'installing our 21st location' with 18-20 coming imminently; 20 used as the most recently confirmed count, with the 21st still in progress.
Exact months to reach current results not stated (joined April 2024, first location end of June 2024, interview ~March 2026); left null rather than estimate.
